source.title: Class-Incremental Continual Learning Into the eXtended DER-Verse
source.authors: Matteo Boschini; Lorenzo Bonicelli; Pietro Buzzega; A. Porrello; S. Calderara

record.file_problem: Supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how trained continual-learning networks’ flatness measures relate to generalization and forgetting, and reports limits on the claimed relation: the evidence concerns continual learning, not the original natural-label generalization setting.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own evaluations of generalization-related performance, secondary information, calibration, and weight-perturbation/Fisher flatness. Cited findings from prior studies are excluded. Figures 7–14 and 16 include plotted results without recoverable exact values; numeric values are recorded only where stated in text or tables. The continual-learning findings are not standard i.i.d. train/test generalization tests.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minimum rationale to explain continual-learning performance, but does not test V7's relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and train/test generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks. Its outcomes are retained accuracy, forgetting, calibration and transfer. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors attribute X-DER's improved continual-learning performance to memory updates and future preparation, and present secondary-information, calibration and flatness analyses as explanations. These analyses do not establish V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship or isolate flatter minima as the cause of X-DER's gains.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies class-incremental continual learning with replay, distillation, task sequences, and future heads; it does not reproduce the original i.i.d. natural-label generalization experiments. Its flatness measurements overlap conceptually with generalization-measure studies but use continual-learning loss and forgetting outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset, memory size, method variant, number of seen tasks, perturbation scale σ, and regularization approach. X-DER’s gains are more pronounced for smaller memory sizes in some comparisons; future-head preparation variants differ in accuracy and forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: X-DER improves final continual-learning accuracy over DER++ across the tested benchmarks; replaying updated logits also improves offline buffer-trained accuracy and calibration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Updating replay logits and preparing future heads can improve class-incremental learning performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-replay methods tolerate magnitude-scaled weight noise better, and X-DER has the lowest reported Fisher traces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replay methods differ in the local geometry of their continual-learning training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: X-DER improves frozen-feature few-shot transfer to unseen classes, with clearer advantages later in the task sequence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Future-head preparation can improve forward transfer in class-incremental learning.

fits_no_version.finding: First-task LFR and LLR regularization improve retained first-task test accuracy after learning a second task across nine adjacent-task pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local loss regularization during an initial task can improve subsequent continual-learning retention.

fits_no_version.finding: X-DER better retains primary-target localization, while distillation methods improve secondary-target recognition and localization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation-based continual learning can preserve visual representations and object localization.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The study concerns continual learning with task shifts, replay buffers, and task-specific future heads, so it does not directly test the listed same-distribution generalization versions. Several supporting results are figure-only with no exact values stated in text. The main benchmark results are reported without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant result rows were left out; V7 is marked tested_not_extracted because its measures concern continual-learning loss and forgetting rather than the train/test gap named in that version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets; using RAdam on CUB-200 supplies no optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects on held-out error; dropout is mentioned as a strategy in prior work, without an own-results comparison.
The association between magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and train/test error gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's T5 classification and V7 tested_not_extracted designation. A different setting alone is not disqualifying; the decisive issue is that the study measures different outcomes. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not claims that the reported continual-learning improvements are unreadable or absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label test generalization.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers trained from scratch.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and other generalization measures were not compared on networks with similarly low training loss; the study measures continual-learning loss and forgetting instead of the V7 train/test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining.
